top_stories.title: AI plagiarised research that passed checks meant to spot it - then I recognised it was my work
top_stories.summary: A researcher describes discovering that AI-generated content had plagiarised their own published work, and that the plagiarism successfully passed through detection systems designed to catch it. The case raises serious concerns about the reliability of AI detection tools and the vulnerability of academic publishing to AI-assisted misconduct. It adds to growing debate about research integrity in an era of generative AI.

top_stories.title: Sam Altman reportedly targeted in second attack
top_stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has reportedly been targeted in a second violent incident, following last week's Molotov cocktail attack on his home. The Verge reports on the escalating pattern of threats against the AI executive as public tensions around AI intensify. The incidents highlight growing personal security risks for prominent figures in the AI industry.

top_stories.title: The AI code wars are heating up
top_stories.summary: The Verge examines the intensifying competition between OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to dominate AI-assisted coding tools, as each major lab races to capture developer loyalty and enterprise contracts. The piece analyses the strategic stakes, product differences, and what the battle means for software development's future. The competition is reshaping how developers work and how AI labs generate revenue.

top_stories.title: Xero & Anthropic fuel AI battle in finance software
top_stories.summary: Accounting software company Xero has partnered with Anthropic to integrate AI capabilities into its finance platform, signalling an intensifying contest to embed large language models into business productivity tools. The deal represents a significant enterprise adoption move for Anthropic's Claude models outside of the tech sector. It reflects broader trends of AI companies competing for dominance in vertical software markets.

top_stories.title: AI Agents Are Coming for Your Dating Life
top_stories.summary: Wired investigates the emerging use of AI agents in online dating, from tools that autonomously manage profiles and send messages to systems that conduct initial conversations on behalf of users. The piece explores the ethical implications of automated romantic interactions and what it means for authenticity and consent in digital relationships. It raises broader questions about AI agents acting on behalf of humans in deeply personal contexts.

further_links.title: Import AI 453: Breaking AI agents; MirrorCode; and ten views on gradual disempowerment
further_links.summary: Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter covers new research on breaking AI agent systems, the MirrorCode project, and ten distinct perspectives on how AI-driven gradual disempowerment might unfold.

further_links.title: AI Will Be Met with Violence, and Nothing Good Will Come of It
further_links.summary: The Algorithmic Bridge examines the social and political conditions that are producing violent responses to AI development and argues that neither the violence nor the industry's trajectory leads to good outcomes.

further_links.title: Why AI Sucks at Front End
further_links.summary: A developer essay argues that AI coding tools perform poorly on front-end web development tasks due to the dynamic, visual, and context-dependent nature of UI work compared to back-end logic.

further_links.title: Apple's accidental moat: How the 'AI Loser' may end up winning
further_links.summary: A Substack analysis argues that Apple's cautious approach to generative AI may ultimately prove to be a competitive advantage, given mounting concerns about privacy, trust, and the backlash facing aggressive AI integrations.

further_links.title: Tech valuations are back to pre-AI boom levels
further_links.summary: Apollo's analysis finds that technology sector valuations have retreated to the levels seen before the generative AI investment surge, raising questions about the durability of AI-driven market enthusiasm.

further_links.title: European AI. A playbook to own it — Mistral
further_links.summary: Mistral AI has published a strategic playbook arguing for European sovereignty in artificial intelligence, outlining how European companies and governments can compete with US and Chinese AI dominance.

further_links.title: How Grok 3 compares to ChatGPT, DeepSeek and other AI rivals
further_links.summary: A comparative analysis benchmarks xAI's Grok 3 model against leading competitors including ChatGPT and DeepSeek across a range of capability and performance tests.

further_links.title: Physical AI Devices to Reach 145 Million Units Over Next Decade
further_links.summary: Counterpoint Research forecasts that physical AI-enabled devices will surge to 145 million units by 2035, driven by robotics, autonomous systems, and edge AI hardware adoption.

further_links.title: What's in a name? Moderna's 'vaccine' vs. 'therapy' dilemma
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review explores how Moderna is navigating the labelling of its mRNA-based cancer treatments, with AI-assisted drug discovery playing a growing role in the company's pipeline development.

further_links.title: AI Hyperscaler Risks 2026: Debt Market Analysis on Oracle, Microsoft, Alphabet
further_links.summary: A debt market analysis examines the financial risks facing major AI hyperscalers Oracle, Microsoft, and Alphabet as they expand AI infrastructure investment amid economic uncertainty.
